title: Meta Muse Explained for Businesses: How the Number One App Shops, Books and Pays on Its Users' Behalf
desc: Meta's Muse agent runs in a secure VM, uses services via API or a browser, and pays with one-time cards. What a local business or store must do to be reachable
keywords: meta muse explained, what is meta muse, meta muse ai agent businesses, muse secure vm sentinel, muse shop pay stripe link, meta muse connectors small business, ai agent booking appointments local business
cta: Want your business to answer when a customer's agent calls?
body:
September 25, 2026. Seventeen days after launch, Meta's Muse is the product every other company in this week's news is reacting to: Amazon blocked it, Shopify wired Shop Pay into it, and Google's stock slid as it climbed the app charts. Meta's September 8 announcement describes a personal agent that does the work rather than answering questions: it opens a browser, fills out forms, negotiates, books travel, lowers a bill and checks out. For a local business, a clinic or an online store, the important sentence is buried in the mechanics. If a service has a public API, Muse connects to it with credentials the user provides; if it has no API, the agent uses the service through a browser the way a person would. That means a customer's agent can already be on your booking page.

How Muse works, from Meta's own description

  1. Muse Secure VM. Each user's agent runs on a dedicated virtual machine in the cloud with its own browser, where the data and credentials for connected services are stored. A separate Sentinel agent on the same machine must approve anything Muse sends to the internet.
  2. Credentials and payment. Meta says Muse has no visibility into passwords or payment methods; credentials go into secure storage it can use without seeing. Checkout runs through Link by Stripe, which issues a one-time-use card and covers purchases with Link's protections, with Shop Pay and 1Password support announced as coming. At Connect on September 23 Meta said Shop Pay is now live and PayPal support has expanded, per TechCrunch.
  3. Approval and audit. Muse checks with the user before sensitive actions such as sending an email or making a purchase, keeps working after the app is closed, and shows a complete audit trail of what it has done and plans to do.
  4. Price and reach. Free for most of what people need, with subscription tiers; available in the US on iOS, Android, muse.ai and WhatsApp, with AI glasses, a Mac desktop mode and a dedicated email address for the agent announced at Connect. Mark Zuckerberg said Meta expects to profit over time by taking a small fee from transactions.
  5. Connectors. Named partners include Shopify, Stripe, PayPal, Best Buy, Gap, Sephora, Walmart, Wayfair, Expedia, GitHub, Notion and Granola, and Meta has opened connector development to outside developers, saying it wants Muse to connect with small businesses too.

Why the browser clause is the one that matters

Every argument this week, including Amazon's decision to block Muse, comes back to that clause. A site with no API does not get to opt in; the agent arrives as a browser session that does not announce itself, fills in the form and pays with a card number the merchant has never seen. Amazon's objection is that an undisclosed third party is moving through customer accounts. A dentist's online booking page, a restaurant's reservation widget or a plumber's quote form has the same exposure and none of Amazon's leverage. The upside is the mirror image: a business whose booking, quoting and ordering can be completed by an agent without a phone call is the business the agent will pick when its user says find me someone who can come Tuesday.

What it means for operators

Decide your agent policy before the traffic decides it for you. Make the transactional pages agent-friendly: a form that completes without a CAPTCHA wall, a clear price, a confirmation the agent can read back to its user, and terms that say what an agent may do. Instrument the site so you can tell agent sessions from human ones. Then close the gap agents cannot cross yet: the phone. Muse books what it can online, but when a service needs a human confirmation, a schedule check or a payment over the phone, the call still has to be answered, and an AI calling agent for home services that picks up, quotes and books around the clock is how a plumber or an HVAC firm gets chosen by a customer whose agent is doing the ringing. Agencies should treat this quarter as the moment to audit every client's transactional surface for agent readiness, because Meta's stated plan is to be in the hands of billions, and the merchants that lose are the ones the agent silently skips.
faqs: Muse is Meta's personal AI agent, launched September 8, 2026, that carries out multi-step tasks such as sending email, booking travel, filling forms and making purchases. It runs on a dedicated secure virtual machine per user, is powered by Meta's Muse Spark model, and is available in the US on iOS, Android, muse.ai and WhatsApp.
How does Muse pay for things?

Through Link by Stripe, which generates a one-time-use card so the user's real card details stay hidden and covers eligible purchases with Link's protections. Meta said at Connect on September 23 that Shop Pay is now available and PayPal support has expanded.
Can Muse use a website that has no API?

Yes. Meta's launch materials say that if a service has no API, Muse can use it through a browser the way a person would, with credentials the user provides. This is the mechanism at the centre of Amazon's decision to block the agent.
What should a small business do about Muse?

Make booking, quoting and ordering pages completable by an agent, publish clear prices and terms, instrument the site to distinguish agent sessions, decide whether to allow or block agents, and make sure the phone is answered around the clock, since agents route to a call when a task cannot finish online.
